Single Tree - Tutorial (RLT)

Ruoqing Zhu

Last Updated: October 27, 2026

Source: vignettes/articles/feature-single-tree.Rmd
feature-single-tree.Rmd

Overview

Use get.one.tree() to inspect the splits and terminal-node predictions in one tree of a fitted forest. The example below fits an unweighted regression forest with both continuous and categorical predictors.

Data

We generate continuous and categorical predictors with a continuous outcome.

set.seed(1)

# ---- Generate a small synthetic dataset ----
n <- 80
p <- 10

# Continuous + categorical predictors (last half as factors)
X1 <- matrix(rnorm(n * (p/2)), n, p/2)
X2 <- matrix(as.integer(runif(n * (p/2)) * 3), n, p/2)  # integers 0,1,2

# Continuous outcome with a simple signal + noise
X_numeric <- data.frame(X1, X2)
colnames(X_numeric) <- paste0("X", seq_len(p))
y <- 1 + rowSums(X_numeric[, 2:6]) +
  2 * (X_numeric[, p/2 + 1] %in% c(1, 2)) + rnorm(n)

X <- X_numeric
X[, (p/2 + 1):p] <- lapply(X[, (p/2 + 1):p], as.factor)

trainX <- X
trainY <- y

Fit 

library(RLT)

fit <- RLT(
  trainX, trainY, model = "regression",
  ntrees = 200, mtry = p/2, nmin = 5,
  resample.prob = 0.8, resample.replace = TRUE,
  nsplit = 0,
  ncores = 1, verbose = FALSE
)

Setting nsplit = 0 searches all available cutpoints for each candidate split variable.

Inspect one tree

Choose a tree number from 1 to the number of fitted trees. This call prints the first tree and invisibly returns a data frame.

get.one.tree(fit, tree = 1)
## Tree #1  [Regression]
## 
## Node  Depth  Split                                Value      n     NodeAve
## ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ 
##     1     0  X6(F)                              12.0000     64      0.0000
##     2     1  X1                                  0.2375     24      0.0000
##     3     1  X4                                  0.1177     40      0.0000
##     4     2  X4                                 -0.5699     17      0.0000
##     5     2  X2                                 -0.1728      7      0.0000
##     6     3  *                                        -      3     -0.8053
##     7     3  X5                                  1.2344     14      0.0000
##     8     4  *                                        -      4      1.2231
##     9     4  X4                                 -0.4458     10      0.0000
##    10     5  *                                        -      4      2.6146
## 
## ... output truncated ...

The preview shows the first few printed rows. Node identifies the node, and Depth counts splits from the root, whose depth is 0. Split names the predictor, with (F) marking a factor and * marking a terminal node. For a continuous split, Value is the cutpoint; for a factor, it encodes a partition of categories and should not be read as a numeric threshold. Terminal nodes display - because they have no split value.

Here n is the number of in-bag observations reaching a node, counting repeated draws. At a terminal node, the printed NodeAve is the mean response used as that leaf’s prediction. The values printed under NodeAve for internal nodes are not node means. The returned data frame contains Node, Depth, Split, Value, and n; NodeAve is part of the printed regression display.
